data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between 'independent' and 'merely uncorrelated' failure modes is only practically resolved by active stress injection across the full network, because passive observation cannot distinguish latent common causes from true independence without a triggered failure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Active stress injection is infeasible at scale","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Latent causes are triggered by rare external events not reproducible in testing","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The failure modes are truly independent and no shared stress triggers them","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Latent common causes (shared configuration errors, latent bugs in common libraries) produce failures that appear uncorrelated until the trigger occurs. Active stress injection (e.g., mutating configurations, pushing resource limits) forces latent causes to manifest, allowing empirical discrimination.
